title: I WILL NOT LET YOU GO

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip so that his hip was wrenched as he wrestled with the man. Then the man said, 'Let me go, for it is daybreak.' But Jacob replied, 'I will not let you go unless you bless me.'" - Gen 32:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The wrestling continues through the night, until with a single touch the mysterious man wrenches Jacob's hip out of joint. In an instant, Jacob is crippled. He cannot win this match now; he can barely stand. Yet in his weakness, he does something remarkable — he clings all the harder and cries, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."

This is a turning point in Jacob's whole life. For decades he had prevailed by grasping and scheming, seizing what he wanted by his own strength and cunning. But now, broken and unable to fight, he prevails in a completely different way — by desperately holding on to God and refusing to let go until he receives a blessing. His strength is gone; only clinging dependence remains.

Here is a deep truth about our life with God. Often it is only when we come to the end of our own strength that we finally learn to cling to Him. God sometimes wounds our self-sufficiency — touches the "hip" we have leaned on — so that we will stop striving in our own power and start clinging to Him in desperate faith.

Are you at the end of your strength? That may be exactly where God wants you — not to crush you, but to teach you the blessing of holding on to Him alone. Do not let go. Cling to God, and refuse to release Him without His blessing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I still trying to prevail by my own strength and scheming?
2. Where has God wounded my self-sufficiency to draw me to cling to Him?
3. What would it mean for me to say, "I will not let You go"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, bring me to the end of my own strength, that I may cling to You alone. When I am weak, teach me to hold on to You in desperate faith and to seek Your blessing above all. Amen.
